newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT-NatMut Asia downgraded.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-NatMut Asia downgraded.

text.p: Asia Equity has cut its rating on National Mutual Asia Ltd (NMA) to a sell from hold, due to the cost and lengthy time required to grow the company's business in China and its current high share price.
"NMA predicts that it will take approximately four years to break even in China with an initial investment of HK$200 million," said analyst Tara Osborough in a recent research note.
Axa-UAP, the French parent of National Mutual Holdings Ltd, has received verbal notification that it will receive a life insurance licence in Shanghai, the report said.
The AXA Group holds a 51 percent in National Mutual Holdings, which holds 53.72 percent of National Mutual Asia directly and another 14.93 percent indirectly.
China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd holds five percent of National Mutual Asia.

"Although there are written and verbal agreements that National Mutual Asia (NMA) will be the vehicle through which Axa-UAP will conduct its China business, this cannot be confirmed yet," the report said.
While the terms of the company's licence in China were still not known, it appeared the company's earnings would be negatively affected in the initial years of its entry into China, it said.

"That said, there is enormous long-term potential in the PRC (People's Republic of China), with PRC insurance sale at 62 billion yuan in financial year 1995 and expected to reach 250 billion yuan by the year 2000," said Osborough.

"We believe that the new appraisal value for NMA with a China licence would be HK$9.33, calculated by pricing its new business (including Hong Kong and the PRC) at a 30 percent premium to the market," the report said.
Osborough has forecast net profit of HK$1.20 billion in 1997 and HK$1.40 billion in 1998.

"We would expect further upside up to HK$10 upon confirmation of NMA's license," the report said. "However, we would recommend to start to take profit now." The share ended the Friday morning session HK$0.15 lower at at HK$8.45.
